title: Move 37 and the chain of thought

questions.prompt: Which part of AlphaGo found Move 37?
feedback: Not alone: the policy network (the intuition) rated Move 37 at 1 in 10,000. Left to itself, it would almost never play it.
Not alone: the search read ahead from moves the policy network proposed, and that network rated this one at 1 in 10,000.
Yes. The intuition gave it a 1 in 10,000 chance; the search read ahead and chose it anyway.

questions.prompt: Is a chain of thought a search?
feedback: Not quite. It can write "wait" and change course, but nothing checks each step, the way AlphaGo's search tested each line.
Not quite. It can backtrack in the text ("Wait, the Pacific is west of Chile.") and be sampled many times and voted on, which is search-like.
Yes, partly: it can change course and be sampled many times, but nothing checks each step. In the trace shown, one unchecked step led to "Water"; the point is on land.

questions.prompt: When Claude 3.7 Sonnet used a hint it was given, how often did its reasoning say so?
feedback: Much lower: about 25% of the time on average (Chen et al., 2025).
Lower: about 25% on average. DeepSeek R1, in the same test, was 39% (Chen et al., 2025).
Right: about 25% of the time on average; DeepSeek R1, 39% (Chen et al., 2025).

questions.prompt: What would make a chain of thought trustworthy?
choices: A record you can check, and checking it
feedback: Longer is the same process: more tokens, each from one pass, and still nothing checking them.
Yes: a record you can inspect, and someone checking it. Both sides of the debate point there; whether that makes it reasoning is the open question.
Size alone does not leave a record you can check; a bigger model's chain of thought is still unchecked.
